title: Shift compatibility of basic strict-system realization operations
statement: Fix $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}k$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $R$ and uniformizer $t$, and $A_n=R/t^n$ for $n\ge1$. For finite-type $k$-schemes $W$ with their small pro-etale sites put $\widehat R_W=\lim_n(A_n)_W$, and let $\mathscr S_W$ be the abelian category of strict semilinear systems of $(A_n)_W$-module sheaves, with its ordinary unbounded derived category, derived reduction $\mathcal R_W$ and total-limit functor $\mathcal L_W=R\lim\operatorname{Res}$ of [lem-coef-derived-system-evaluation-calculus]; regard $\mathscr S_W$ as the module category of the ring diagram $((A_n)_W)_n$ on the simultaneous ringed diagram site of [lem-sf-integral-compactification-system-realization]. Use the system operations of that statement: exact system inverse image $P_v$ for separated finite-type $v$, total derived system direct image $S_p$ for proper $p$, exact termwise open extension $J_j$ for quasi-compact open $j$, and derived system tensor; their integral counterparts are completed pullback, integral proper direct image, localized completed open extension and completed tensor. Restrict all input and intermediate systems to normalized systems with compatible etale-origin witnesses, bounded constructible cohomology and finite Tor amplitude in common finite intervals; integral inputs $K_i$ are derived complete and constructible. Let $A$ be one basic operation $P_v$, $S_p$, $J_j$ or derived tensor. Let $d_A$ be exactly the single-operation comparison specified in [lem-sf-generator-reduction-coherence], namely the canonical reduction-tower realization comparison from $\mathcal L_WA(\mathcal R_WK_i)$ (with two inputs for tensor) to the corresponding completed integral operation, with $\mathcal L_W$ computed by the Roos total-cone model of [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-strict-tower-homotopy-limit]. The ringed-diagram-site models give termwise/K-injective/K-flat integer-shift comparisons for these operations. For every integer $r$ and every chosen input slot, the square for $d_A$ commutes naturally; in the tensor case the comparison in the shifted slot includes the Koszul sign. The comparisons on each integral basic operation are natural in its input morphisms and coherent for addition of shifts. The same is true for the system operations and for the total-limit comparison occurring on the source side of $d_A$.
